newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-KLEIN, WEBB SHARE THREE-SHOT LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KLEIN, WEBB SHARE THREE-SHOT LEAD.

text.p: Emilee Klein and Australian rookie Karrie Webb shared a three-stroke lead after three rounds of the inaugural $700,000 LPGA Tour Championship Saturday.
The 22-year-old Klein, who held the lead entering the round, fired a two-under-par 70 to move to nine under. Webb, who is battling Britain's Laura Davies for the money title, carded a 68.
Davies, who leads the LPGA with four wins this season, was among five golfers at six under. Davies and McGann, a three-time winner in 1996, fired 71s.
Juli Inkster, who entered the day one shot behind Klein, shot a 72 and Hall of Famer Nancy Lopez and Brandie Burton both shot 69s to also stand at 210.
Pat Hurst, still seeking her first career LPGA victory, tied a course record by firing a 65 to join Kelly Robbins at five under, four strokes off the pace.
Jane Geddes, Briton Caroline Pierce and Penny Hammel were six strokes back.

Davies, who has clinched the 1996 Player of the Year Award, leads Webb in 1996 earnings by $45,302. Either one could become the first LPGA player to earn more than $1 million in a season by winning the $150,000 first prize here.
